name: turbo_c_large_huge
description: Turbo C large code/data model with huge-qualified image pointers for buffers crossing 64 KiB boundaries
compile_command: tcc -ml -c fax_core.c fax_engine.c fax_g3.c fax_tables.c fax_thread.c fax_default_params.c
notes: Public image pointers and image-sized workspace pointers are huge-qualified so row traversal can cross segment boundaries.
The library sources are compiled as objects; the convenience test driver is intentionally excluded because its malloc-based workspace allocator is not a DOS huge-memory allocator.
The host application must allocate every huge workspace array with a Turbo C-compatible huge allocator and assign the pointers explicitly.
The small dither row buffers are also huge-qualified for a uniform API; their individual size remains far below 64 KiB at fax widths.
This profile has not been compiled with Turbo C in the current environment; verify the exact compiler release and memory-model switches.
The full optimizer needs about 11 bytes per input pixel plus fixed workspace; conventional DOS memory is insufficient for a full fax page without EMS/XMS or a reduced working raster.
The optimizer and image transforms use C math functions (pow, exp, sqrt, floor, fmod); link the compiler math library/runtime.
The optional fax_image.c host adapter has built-in PGM/BMP readers only unless codec libraries are supplied. Modern PNG/JPEG/TIFF libraries are not part of the Turbo C core-only build.
The optimizer API consumes a caller-owned grayscale raster directly; a DOS host can supply its own file decoder or omit file I/O entirely.
compiler_version_target: Turbo C 2.x/3.x family; confirm huge pointer support
endianness: native compiler target; no byte-order assumptions in the core
